summary.en: Turkish forces are remaining in Syria and Iraq until border security is assured, while the Syrian defence minister reiterates the deployment. DNA testing has identified the remains of seven family members, offering hope to families of the missing, and 600 displaced Syrian families are preparing to return home. The US special envoy praised General Mazloum Abdi for integrating Syrian military units, and the Syrian court continues trials of three defendants in transitional-justice cases. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Tyrkiske styrker blir i Syria og Irak til grense sikkerheten er sikret, mens den syriske forsvarsministeren gjentar innsettingen. DNA-testing har identifisert restene av syv familiemedlemmer, noe som gir håp til familier med savnede, og 600 fordrevet syriske familier forbereder seg på å vende hjem. USAs spesialutsending roste general Mazloum Abdi for å integrere syriske militærenheter, og den syriske domstolen fortsetter rettssakene mot tre tiltalte i saker om overgangsrettferdighet. UCDP registrerte 2 732 døde i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
